data.narrative:
Theion, a Series A–stage climate and energy company founded by Ulrich Ehmes, has raised €25M+ to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector includes nine peer companies at various stages, comprising one public entity (LNZA) and eight private firms including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen. However, the peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with similar valuation tiers—fewer than three datapoints meet narrow filtering criteria—limiting the applicability of median peer multiples to this analysis.

The primary valuation method applied is Stage-Progression, which uses total capital raised (€25M proxy) as a base and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage advancement. This approach yields an implied valuation of $50M. A sensitivity range accounting for variance around this single-method estimate places the low bound at $42M (15% discount) and high bound at $57M (15% premium). This range reflects the inherent uncertainty of extrapolating from one method rather than triangulation across multiple independent approaches.

Key uncertainties include the absence of granular peer multiples at Theion's specific stage and the reliance on a broad stage-progression multiplier that may not capture sector-specific capital efficiency or market conditions in frontier climate technology. Additional revenue visibility, burn trajectory, or competitive positioning data would strengthen conviction in this range.
